Though this matter has come up for admission,
with consent of learned counsel for parties, it is taken up for hearing.
2. This appeal is filed against the judgment and award dated 13.10.2021 passed by the Principal Senior Civil Judge and Kalaburagi, in MVC No.1083 of 2019.
NC: 2025:KHC-K:7474 HC-KAR 3.
The injured claimant, aged 28 years, doing private work met with an accident on 23.02.2019 and filed a claim application claiming compensation of Rs.16,26,000/-.
The Tribunal, considering the entire evidence on record, granted the compensation of Rs.5,60,000/- with interest at the rate of 6 percent per annum from the date of petition till realisation.

sentences.text: Aggrieved by the said order, this appeal is preferred by the appellant-claimant in which it is mainly contended that he sustained fracture of left tibia and fibula and took treatment from 23.02.2019 to 02.03.2019 for 8 days.

Exhibit P7 is the disability certificate issued by the doctor,
where the doctor assessed the disability as 52.33% to the whole body, but the tribunal has taken only 13%.
He was earning Rs.18,000/- per month, but the tribunal has taken Rs.13,250/- per month.
The amounts granted under other heads are meager.
Therefore, requested for enhancement.
5. Heard the arguments of both sides.
6. The injured claimant has not filed any income proof to show that he was earning Rs.18,000/- per month.

As he met NC: 2025:KHC-K:7474 HC-KAR with the accident in the year 2019, the tribunal has rightly taken the notional income of Rs.13,250/- per month as per the guidelines of the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority, and it needs no interference.
His age was taken as 28 years as per Exhibit P13-Adhar card and the multiplier as 17.
The petitioner examined the doctor as PW2 and the doctor issued Exhibit P7 disability certificate assessing the disability as 52.33%.
One third of 52.33% disability comes to 17%.
Therefore the disability assessed by the Tribunal is to be modified.

Thus, the loss of future earning capacity comes to Rs.4,59,510/- (13,250 x 12 x 17 x 17%).
7.

Considering the occupation of the petitioner, nature of injuries, period of hospitalization, this Court finds it reasonable to grant Rs.60,000/- for pain and suffering, Rs.30,000/- for loss of amenities and Rs.30,000/- for transportation, extra nourishment and attendant charges.
The petitioner might not have attended any other job at least for a period of four months.

Therefore,
Rs.53,000/- (13250x4) is granted for the loss of income during laid up period.
The doctor-PW2 has stated that the petitioner requires another surgery for removal of NC: 2025:KHC-K:7474 HC-KAR implants and estimated the cost of surgery as between Rs.70,000/- and Rs.80,000/-.
Therefore, this Court finds it reasonable to grant an amount of Rs.50,000/- for future medical expenses.
Tribunal granted Rs.82,495/- towards medical expenses and it needs no interference.
Thus, in all, the claimant is entitled for the compensation of Rs.7,65,005/- with interest at 6% per annum as against Rs.5,60,000/- awarded by the Tribunal.

8. The award of compensation passed by the Tribunal is modified as under:

As it is the case of no driving licence, the Tribunal directed the insurance company to pay and recover.
Therefore, this Court finds it reasonable to direct the respondent-insurance company to pay and recover from the owner of the vehicle.

10. In the result, the following order is passed:
 (i) Appeal is allowed in part.
( ii) The Claimant is entitled for the total compensation of Rs.7,65,005/- with interest at 6 percent per annum from the date of petition till the date of realization.

(iii) The respondent insurance company has already deposited the award amount before the Tribunal, and therefore, they are directed to deposit the enhanced amount of Rs.2,05,005/- with interest at 6% per annum within one month from the date of this order.
(iv) On such deposit, the claimant is permitted to withdraw the entire amount along with the interest accrued on it.
NC: 2025:KHC-K:7474 HC-KAR (v) The respondent-insurance company is at liberty to recover the said amount on the owner of the vehicle by due process of law.
